questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Paris was the perfect destination for me both personally and academically. I study Modern Culture and I am therefore very interested in culture and the cultural offerings in Paris are abundant. Moreover, I was contemplating moving to Paris after my studies so my exchange also helped me make that descision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the uni admin stuff is difficult and there was not much help from KU's side. France is known for its bureaucracy which was also demonstrated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Just emailed the coordinator at Sorbonne Nouvelle

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lot's of information - maybe to much to keep track of.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The coordinatrice answers really quickly

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Cité Universitaire is great

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Paris rent is expensive, but it's much more affordable to live at the City. Also you will live in a 'kollegie' so you can make friends with people from all over the world studying different things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very old school. First year they switched to online application so naturally the application system crashed and was down for a few days. Lot's of going back and forth with teacher and administration. Did end up getting all my classes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to find the timetables for the classes and then register either online or in person. It's a mess so also just show up to all the classes you want to take and talk to the professor.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Lot's of different admin branches to contact - there is also an Erasmus help desk in the Lobby all semester!!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all of my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the Erasmus help desk

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing professor for three courses. For my other classes one professor was really nice but I did not like her way of overanalysing literature. The last professor was, in her own words, "a bit bonkers" - really boring but thought she was funny - did not want us to do academic work for our exam?!?!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Liked my classes overall. Loved three of them but did not care for the other three. The classes are insanely specific and nothing like the generalised 15 ects classes at KU that doesn't really go into depth at all. These go very much, and some of them a bit too much, into depth. 

Dropped one of the specific erasmus classes intended to improve your french skills and knowledge of France, because the teacher did not want to teach and told us it would be student presentation the entire semester. VERY LAZY!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was much more like folkeskole tbh. Boring classroom teaching, weird child/adult dynamic between professor and students - even at masters level. Kind of odd.
Had an English teacher and his way of teaching was similar to KU, except that the students did not engage very much and were obviously used to adult/child dynamic from their other courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
M7IC201 TD 01 Médiacultures,
A7SL401 Dissident Bodies in Contemporary Art, 
A9SL203 Virginia Woolf - The Waves,
C9MG007 Queer Studies : Identités, Sexualités, Représentations(ang),
M9IC201 TD 01 Industrie et culture de la mode,
A9SL401 Writing Shame

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any class taught by Nick Rees-Roberts - he is a really good teacher and incredibly knowledgable in cultural, film, fashion, and gender studies.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Train was more expensive than expected - but I also only bike in Copenhagen. You can bike here but I would not dare to do it myself - have seen 3 bike accidents (car or scooter driving into cyclist) while here because they are not yet used to bikes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offered a lot which I could tell by the 15 emails I received daily. Did not go to any of them tho. Except for a film club

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had sports classes, lots of art stuff. Student based clubs and activities. No student bar though

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The film club was fun. Met a lot of people, watched good movies, they also had panel discussions with actors and filmmakers.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use the city - museums are free for under 26 yo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in class

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language probably. A lot of people don't want to speak french with you because they can hear that you are not native and therefore assume that you don't understand it very well. At other times when you really don't understand some people will not try to speak english or simplify it for you. Very mixed bag really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The art museums and the general focus on good art everywhere. Whether that be street art, graphic design, posters, architecture etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If in doubt email the Erasmus coordinatrice or ask at one of the help desks. 
Classroom culture is very weird. Students are either patronised or cruel towards each other when it comes to criticism after presentations (there will be a lot of those) and they do not know what constructive criticism is.
You have to bring your own pen and paper to the exam - did not know you had to bring your own paper and the teacher was annoyed that they had to go get some for the exchange students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will be able to take really nerdy specific classes, but the academic level is not very high - but that is nice because then you don't have to study to hard and have more time to have fun in Paris.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends I've made and the three classes I took that I was really interested in and wanted to take before my exchange as KU does not offer anything like them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language, all the bureaucracy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Download the app shotgun so you can see what events and parties are happening - you often need to book a ticket. Also if you book a ticket for a nightclub and arrive before 12 it's usually free (otherwise is can be very expensive)

Make a google maps over places to see and go and add every time you walk past something that looks nice.

Go on a croissant tour - there is a croissant tour video on youtube - fun way to explore the different arrondissements.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
